verdict.rationale: Blaxel provides cloud-hosted sandboxes built for running code, so execution happens off your own infrastructure. You can run shell commands and processes inside them via SDK or MCP. The docs also describe concrete hardening: per-domain egress allowlists and denylists to prevent data exfiltration, a proxy-based firewall, running workloads as an unprivileged non-root user, and time-limited scoped session tokens. Missing for 10: no documentation of the underlying isolation boundary (e.g., microVM or kernel-level separation between tenants), no explicit framing for untrusted code, and no independent or hands-on corroboration of the security claims.
